explanation: Relational division asks which targets are related to every item in a source set. A vendor qualifies only if no required part is missing, which can be tested with nested non-existence or with grouped counts over the required set.

options.text: Use a correlated NOT EXISTS query that checks for missing required parts for each vendor, or an equivalent grouped COUNT(DISTINCT part_id) comparison against all three required IDs.
Use EXISTS with one required part ID, because one match implies all three are covered.
Use UNION between the three part IDs and the vendor list, because UNION keeps only common rows.
Use a three-table join and return vendors that have at least one of the required parts.

prompt: A vendor database has Vendors(vendor_id, vendor_name), Parts(part_id, part_name), and Supplies(vendor_id, part_id). You need the vendors who supply every part in a required list of three part IDs: 11, 12, and 13. Which approach is the best match for this requirement?
